subject: BYO key rotation SLA & log-sampling clarification
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Eva Morales <eva.morales@finapi.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Aug 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: BYO key rotation SLA & log-sampling clarification

Hi Eva — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap of what we captured and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the right PO/contract language: 

1) BYO keys preference: you indicated FinAPI would prefer to bring your own customer-managed keys (BYOK) and have Redwood support both monthly rotation (triggered by your KMS) and the option for HSM-backed key wrapping for higher assurance. Confirming: is the requirement that the cryptographic root (wrapping key) remain in your KMS/HSM and not be exported to Redwood at any point?

2) Rotation SLA: you asked whether Redwood can attest to timely rotation without service interruption. We propose a rolling rewrap flow where new key material is staged and KV cache re-encrypted with a <5 minute expected rewrap window. We will document fallback to a compatible hosted key variant if BYOK rewrap is delayed beyond a configured tolerance. Is a 15-minute hard-fail window acceptable for your security ops team, or do you need automated failover to the hosted variant immediately at rotation time?

3) Logging & sampling: requirement was to capture key-usage audit events (encrypt/decrypt/unwrap/wrap) and surface them via an audit log stream; you mentioned sampling for low-risk telemetry. Can you confirm the minimum retention for sampled logs vs. full audit logs for key ops (e.g., 90 days sampled, 1 year full for key admin events)? Also let us know if logs must be sent to your SIEM (we support Syslog/S3/Kafka endpoints).

4) In-transit/at-rest: Redwood enforces TLS1.3 for in-transit. At rest we use AES-256-GCM for model artifacts and a separate envelope encryption approach for customer material. I attached a short BYO options doc + diagram and an evidence checklist.

Next steps we propose: (a) send the redwood-byo-key-options.pdf and an evidence matrix (attached) for your security review (attached), (b) schedule a 30-min technical sync with your cloud security engineer to verify key placement and network egress constraints, (c) draft a contract addendum for BYOK rotation SLA language.

Action items: 
- Eva: confirm (i) absolute non-export requirement for wrapping key, (ii) log retention minima and SIEM endpoint preference.
- Naomi: draft rotation SLA language and propose failover window.
- Aditya: prepare a brief on operational rewrap flow and expected latency impact.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood-byo-key-options.pdf, evidence_matrix.xlsx, key_rotation_diagram.png)

From: Eva Morales <eva.morales@finapi.com>

Subject: Re: BYO key rotation SLA & log-sampling clarification

Thanks Naomi — helpful recap. A few answers below: 

1) Correct, the wrapping key (root/key encryption key) must remain in our HSM-backed KMS (Cloud HSM). No exports.

2) Rotation SLA: security requires no silent failures. Our preference is automatic failover to hosted variant only after a 10-minute detection window + manual acknowledgement by our ops team; if you can support a configurable detection window up to 10 minutes that would be ideal. We want telemetry to alert on rewrap failures.

3) Logs: for key usage we need full audit logs (encrypt/decrypt/unwrap/wrap) retained 1 year. For verbose telemetry (token-level sampling, internal perf traces) 90-day sampling is fine. We will forward SIEM to an S3 bucket; sending to S3 is preferred.

4) Please include a short runbook for on-call steps during rotation failures (who to page, what to escalate).

We'll coordinate a tech call with our cloud security engineer — availability next Wed/Thu afternoon PST.

Eva Morales
Head of Security
FinAPI

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Hi Eva — technical notes to clarify what the PoC will exercise: 

- BYOK modes: we support KMS-only (customer KMS hosted in-cloud with API-based rewrap) and HSM-wrapping (customer-managed HSM that performs wrap/unwrap operations; Redwood never stores raw wrapping key). For HSM, we use an asymmetric wrap key so that lifecycle operations are fully non-exportable.

- Rewrap flow: to keep latency low we do an online rewrap for KV cache and rotate new keys for blob stores in the background. For long-running requests we preserve KV cache behavior to avoid client-visible failures during a single request; rewraps will affect new sessions. Expect a 1–3 second per-request overhead at the moment of key switch for cache misses.

- Audit/log delivery: we can push key-op events to S3 (preferred by FinAPI), and also stream summarized metrics to your SIEM via Kafka if you want near-real-time dashboards. Full audit retention 1 year can be supported; we will include HIPAA/SOC2 evidence where applicable.

I'll prepare a short checklist for the tech sync and a minimal PoC runbook.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
